Prune loci based on a Linkage Disequilibrium threshold, as PLINK

Source: R/loci_ld_prune.R
loci_ld_prune.Rd

This function prunes loci in LD as plink --indep-pairwise (PLINK 1.9) does, and returns the same loci. A window of window_size loci (or of window_size kb, with window_in_kb = TRUE) moves along each chromosome by step_size loci. Within each window, pairs of loci whose squared correlation (r^2) is above thr_r2 are found in order, and the locus with the lower minor allele frequency of each pair is removed (the later one when their frequencies are equal), until no such pair remains. Loci with no variance (e.g. monomorphic loci) are removed, as in PLINK; but, also as in PLINK, a locus alone on its chromosome, or alone in the first window of its chromosome (with a window in kb), is kept even if it has no variance. Clumping (loci_ld_clump()) gives a better spread of loci along the chromosomes.

Usage

loci_ld_prune(.x, .col = "genotypes", ...)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_df'
loci_ld_prune(.x, .col = "genotypes", ...)

# S3 method for class 'vctrs_bigSNP'
loci_ld_prune(
  .x,
  .col = "genotypes",
  window_size,
  step_size,
  thr_r2,
  window_in_kb = FALSE,
  min_shared = 2,
  insufficient = c("keep", "remove"),
  n_cores = 1,
  return_id = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

.x

a gen_tibble object

.col

the column to be used when a tibble (or grouped tibble is passed directly to the function). This defaults to "genotypes" and can only take that value. There is no need for the user to set it, but it is included to resolve certain tidyselect operations.

...

currently not used.

window_size

the size of the window: a number of loci (at least 2), or, with window_in_kb = TRUE, a distance in kb.

step_size

the number of loci by which the window moves (PLINK recommends 1 with windows in kb). With a window of a number of loci, it should not be larger than window_size.

thr_r2

the threshold of r^2 above which two loci are linked (at least 0, and less than 1).

window_in_kb

boolean: is window_size a distance in kb (TRUE), or a number of loci (FALSE, the default)?

min_shared

the minimum number of individuals genotyped at both loci for their r^2 to be used. Default is 2, as in PLINK (with fewer, r^2 is undefined).

insufficient

what to do with pairs of loci genotyped together in fewer than min_shared individuals: "keep" (the default) both loci, or "remove" the one with the lower minor allele frequency, as if they were linked.

n_cores

number of cores to be used (to read the genotypes; the pruning itself runs on one core, as in PLINK)

return_id

boolean on whether the id of SNPs to keep should be returned. It defaults to FALSE, which returns a vector of booleans (TRUE or FALSE)

Value

a boolean vector indicating whether each locus is kept (as the loci of plink --indep-pairwise in the .prune.in file), or a vector of the indices of the loci kept (with return_id = TRUE)

Details

Missing genotypes do not need to be imputed: as in PLINK, r^2 is the squared correlation of the allele counts of two loci over the individuals genotyped at both. Pairs of loci genotyped together in fewer than min_shared individuals have no reliable r^2: by default, they are not considered linked (as in PLINK, for which r^2 is then undefined); with insufficient = "remove", the locus with the lower minor allele frequency is removed, as if they were linked. Imputed genotypes are used only if the gen_tibble is set to use them (see gt_set_imputed()).

Differences from PLINK: all individuals are used (PLINK uses only founders); all chromosomes are treated as autosomes (PLINK treats the sex chromosomes of males as haploid); and loci on chromosome "0" (unplaced) are pruned as those of any other chromosome, whereas PLINK ignores them and lists them in neither its .prune.in nor its .prune.out file (so that --extract with .prune.in drops them, but --exclude with .prune.out keeps them).

References

Chang C.C. et al. (2015) Second-generation PLINK: rising to the challenge of larger and richer datasets. GigaScience 4: 7.

See also

loci_ld_clump() for clumping.

Examples

# (the example has missing genotypes, which do not need to be imputed)
example_gt <- load_example_gt("gen_tbl")

# as plink --indep-pairwise 4 1 0.2
example_gt %>% loci_ld_prune(window_size = 4, step_size = 1, thr_r2 = 0.2)
#> [1]  TRUE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE
# the indices of the loci kept
example_gt %>%
  loci_ld_prune(window_size = 4, step_size = 1, thr_r2 = 0.2,
    return_id = TRUE
  )
#> [1] 1 2 4 5
